[Date]

Wellpoint Appeals Department  
[Submission address or fax number from the appeal instructions]

Re: Appeal of denial of total ankle replacement  
Member: Avery Hayes  
Member ID: W671125198  
Plan: Wellpoint Commercial/ACA, Georgia  
Reference number: POC-1F29AC6C03-84154  
Requested service: Total ankle replacement  
CPT: 27702  
Date of denial notice: August 9, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Wellpoint’s denial of the requested total ankle replacement. The stated reason for denial is that the submitted clinical records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery.

The records document a substantial and unsuccessful course of conservative treatment:

- I have experienced 18 months of progressive ankle pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months, with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 8, 2026. It provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- I completed 24 supervised physical-therapy visits from May 8, 2026, through July 3, 2026. Therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance, and the physical-therapy discharge note documents completion of this treatment course.
- Despite these measures, I continue to have significant pain and functional limitation. I walk with an antalgic gait and can ambulate only approximately two blocks. Range of motion is limited by pain, and provocative testing remains positive on the affected side.

The clinical records also document objective disease consistent with the requested procedure. Weight-bearing ankle radiographs obtained on July 13, 2026, showed obliteration of the tibiotalar joint space with subchondral cysts. These findings, together with the prolonged symptoms, failed medication treatment, limited response to injection, completed supervised therapy, abnormal gait, restricted walking tolerance, and painful limited motion, support medical necessity for total ankle replacement.

There are no documented clinical barriers identified in the packet that would make the procedure inappropriate. The records state that there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI is 29, and the patient is a nonsmoker. The procedure was requested by Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery.

The public policy materials I was able to retrieve did not establish which specific Wellpoint Georgia policy or clinical guideline was applied to this determination. The plan has not been quoted because the denial notice did not identify the governing document, policy number, version, effective date, or the specific components and duration of the required conservative-treatment trial.

Please perform a full appeal review of the enclosed records and reverse the denial. If Wellpoint maintains the denial, please provide the exact medical-necessity policy or clinical utilization-management guideline applied to CPT 27702, including its title, document or policy number, version or effective date, complete criteria, and a detailed explanation identifying which documented requirement remains unsatisfied.

Please also provide the clinical-review rationale and the qualifications of the reviewing clinician. I request that the appeal be reviewed by an orthopedic specialist or other clinician with appropriate expertise in ankle reconstruction.

Enclosures:

1. Denial notice dated August 9, 2026  
2. Physical-therapy discharge note documenting 24 completed visits from May 8, 2026, through July 3, 2026  
3. Medication and treatment history documenting eight months of NSAID use and the May 8, 2026, corticosteroid injection  
4. July 13, 2026, weight-bearing ankle radiograph report  
5. Orthopedic examination and clinical notes  
6. Any additional records submitted by Duval, MD

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and notify me of the appeal decision in writing.

Sincerely,

Avery Hayes
